newsitem.title: USA: Chung lawyer defends Asian American donor.
newsitem.headline: Chung lawyer defends Asian American donor.

text.p: A lawyer for Democratic Party donor Johnny Chung said in a television interview on Wednesday the California businessman had never acted as a conduit to funnel foreign money to the U.S. political system.

The lawyer, Brian Sun, also told CNN in an interview that he regretted the "rush to judgment" by the Democratic National Committee (DNC), the party's main institution, in returning money Chung had donated.
Asked whether any of the money had come from China, Sun replied" "absolutely not," adding that any suggestion Chung acted "as a conduit for foreign money is absolutely untrue."

Chung is one of several Asian American figures in the fund-raising controversy that has engulfed President Bill Clinton and his Democratic Party and is the subject of probes by the Justice Department and congressional committees.
Last month the DNC announced it was returning $1.5 million in questionable donations, bringing the total of such contributions that it has given back to nearly $3 million.
Of this, officials have said more than three quarters was raised by Chung, former Democratic fundraiser and Commerce Department official John Huang and Arkansas businessman Charles Yah Lin Trie.
Chung's role has come under particular scrutiny following the disclosure that he gave a $50,000 donation at the White House to Maggie Willians, the chief of staff to Clinton's wife Hillary.

Taking contributions at the White House is illegal, but the White House has argued that Williams did not technically "accept or receive" the check, but simply passed it on and therefore did nothing wrong.
Sun told CNN Chung, who visited the White House more than 50 times during the past four years, had no prior relationship with Clinton or his wife but was an "ardent admirer."

The lawyer said Chung believed his donations may have helped win access but said there was never any explicit quid pro quo and that noone at the White House or the DNC had ever said: "if you make a donation you will get A,B or C in return."
